The laws of the gambit

Win: eliminate all enemies or leave them with no legal move. Clear five sectors and defeat the Boss Commander. Each victory restores your eight-piece army; class upgrades and your ten-card deck persist.

Move: amber is yours. Select a piece, then a green destination. Pawns move and capture diagonally forward. Kings move and capture both ways. Reaching the far rank crowns a piece and ends its move.

Mandatory captures: if any unfrozen piece can jump, you must jump. After a capture, the same piece must continue while jumps remain. A move ends the turn automatically. End turn passes only when no jump is required.

Berserker ✦: standard jumps plus diagonal three-square leaps over exactly one enemy, with all other squares clear. All classes chain ordinary captures.

Necromancer ☠: each captured enemy becomes a friendly one-hit Skeleton on the captured square. Skeletons are ordinary forward-moving pawns and may become kings.

Shield-Guard ⛨: begins each battle with one shield. The first attempted jump breaks the shield, leaves both pieces in place, and spends the attacker's turn. Iron Crown can restore a shield to any ally.

Spells: draw three from your ten-card deck every player turn; unused cards are discarded and the discard pile reshuffles as needed. Refill to 3 MP each turn; battle opening starts at 2 MP (3 with Archmage). Cast before moving. Purple outlines mark valid targets. Spell kills do not trigger necromancy.

Terrain: Rifts block empty dark squares for two enemy turns. Frost Traps last three enemy turns and freeze an enemy that lands on them, preventing its next move. Time Lock freezes a targeted enemy in the same way. An entirely frozen army loses a turn, not the battle.

Routes: Skirmish fields fewer enemies; Bastion adds Shield-Guards; Warforge adds Berserkers. The boss fields twelve pieces and starts with two kings.

Draft: replace one card, keeping exactly ten, or permanently train one army slot in a class. After 80 rounds, higher material wins (king 2, other piece 1, shield +0.25); ties favor the defender. Three repeated positions are adjudicated the same way.

Saving: progress saves on this browser after each action. Audio begins only after you enable it. Archmage preview is a local preference, not verified subscription access.
